summary: The adopt CLI and its tests are broadly sound, but default-branch resolution falls back to a literal 'main' that is never checked, so a declared adoption shape breaks and an FR-007 refusal is bypassed; one declared failure path has no test, and the write's failure handling and commit bookkeeping need fixing.

findings.summary: default_base() returns the literal branch name 'main' without checking that it exists, so in a repo with no origin/HEAD and a non-main default branch the dry run reports base 'main', a default-branch source dies with exit 2, and a spec dir held only on local 'main' is accepted with no FR-007 refusal.
findings.evidence: Reproduced in a scratch repo (default branch master, pushed to origin, origin/HEAD unset, no local main). A branch-shape dry run for 007-x printed base 'main' although origin/master exists. A dry run for 008-y, whose spec dir exists only on origin/master, exited 2 with 'factory: fatal: Not a valid object name main' (adopt.py _resolve line 69 runs ls-tree on the missing ref through commands.git, which dies). A spec dir committed only on local 'main' (009-z) returned shape default-branch with refusal null, where spec.md FR-007 requires the refusal 'spec dir is on local <default> but not on <base>'. The write re-inspects with the pending base, which SKILL.md step 2 sets to origin/<default>, so the clean dry run is followed after the grill by a misleading 'no branch or spec dir matches' refusal. spec.md Assumptions say base and the default branch are 'resolved as for a new run', and SKILL.md step 2 uses origin/<default> (gh, else main); research.md D3 instead falls back to a literal main, so two rules govern the same knowledge (ENG-6). The existing tests (test_branch_shape_prints_the_report_and_exits_0 asserting base 'main', and OtherShapeTests with origin/main) never exercise origin/HEAD or a non-main default, so the defect is untested (ENG-1).
findings.fix: Resolve the default branch the same way SKILL.md step 2 does, or take the orchestrator's base as input. Verify each candidate ref with show-ref before use, and never use a local branch name for default-branch resolution: refuse with a named reason when no origin default resolves. Add tests for origin/HEAD unset with a non-main default branch, for the default-branch shape there, and for a local-only spec dir there (expects the FR-007 refusal).

findings.summary: The exit-3 path for several matching spec dirs (in _resolve) and for a branch that adds several spec dirs (in _spec_dir) has no asserting test, although plan.md's confirmed dry-run seam declares it as a failure path.
findings.evidence: adopt.py lines 69-71 (_resolve: len(dirs) > 1 -> die(3)) and lines 95-96 (_spec_dir: 'adds several spec dirs' -> die(3)) add behaviour. tools/tests/test_adopt.py has one exit-3 test, test_ambiguous_source_exits_3_listing_both_branches (line 390), which covers several matching branches only. plan.md Test seams declares for the dry-run seam 'several matching spec dirs exit 3 listing them', and the plan's Confirmed line (Q2 accepted) lists that failure path as in scope. Behaviour with no asserting test is HIGH under ENG-1, and the confirmed seam scope is unmet.
findings.fix: Add tests in DryRunReportTests or OtherShapeTests: two spec dirs matching the same name on base (for example specs/007-x and specs/008-x with no branch) exit 3, list both, and leave the snapshot unchanged. Add a second test for a branch that adds two spec dirs under specs/, which must also exit 3 and write nothing.

findings.summary: The adopt write's failure handling has three defects: post-commit cleanup runs inside the rollback try, so a failed unlink rolls back a landed adoption commit; a git failure in 'worktree add' escapes outside the try as exit 2 with no rollback; and _rollback ignores git's exit codes while the CLI still reports 'rolled back'.
findings.evidence: _record_worktree_run runs commands.commit_worktree and then pending.unlink() (line 286, no missing_ok). Both run inside _adopt_worktree's try, which catches OSError (lines 241-245) and calls _rollback, which removes the worktree and any branch the write created. _rollback (lines 297-305) runs git with capture_output and never checks returncode, yet the CLI prints 'adopt failed and was rolled back'. The 'worktree add' calls (lines 234-239) sit outside the try; commands.git dies with code 2, not the exit 1 that contracts/cli.md line 28 documents for a failed step. ENG-17, ENG-26.
findings.fix: Make the commit the last fallible step in the try. Move the pending and sidecar unlink after the try with missing_ok, reporting leftovers as a warning rather than a rollback. Check _rollback's return codes and name any leftover worktree or branch in the error. Wrap worktree-add failures so they exit 1 after cleanup, as contracts/cli.md states.

findings.summary: The CLI's no-pending-adoption error names the harness invocation '/factory adopt', which puts a harness-specific command into core/ code and contradicts the stated rule that the CLI names its own verb.
findings.evidence: Constitution Principle II: files under core/ MUST NOT name a harness tool, path or command. research.md D9: 'The CLI names its own verb; the skill names the harness invocation.' Line 208 says "run `/factory adopt {src}`". The resume hint added in commands.py uses the bare verb 'adopt <branch|spec_dir>', so the two CLI hints disagree. Design guidance, so the severity ceiling applies.
findings.fix: Change the message to name the CLI verb, for example "no pending adoption '{name}'; start it with adopt {src}", matching the resume hint's wording.

findings.summary: Commit fb2d038 (T012) ticks T013's checkbox in tasks.md before T013's work exists in 854aea9, so the history records T013 as done one commit early. This is disclosed and the final tree is correct.
findings.evidence: git show fb2d038 -- specs/022-adopt-spec/tasks.md flips both T012 and T013 from [ ] to [x]. The T013 commit 854aea9 touches only the role files, not tasks.md. ENG-3 requires each unit's task status to be checked in the same passing commit as its implementation.
findings.fix: Do not rewrite history. The approver may accept the disclosed early check, and the retro should record it.

findings.summary: The T014 and T015 commits (3d3bfce, 736b480) cite 'Exempt: verification only (ENG-5; plan.md Test seams)', but plan.md declares no such exemption.
findings.evidence: plan.md's Test seams Exempt line lists only documentation files. Neither task changes behaviour, so ENG-1 and ENG-2 do not apply, but ENG-5 exemptions must be stated in the plan.
findings.fix: No history rewrite. Either add a verification-only line to the plan's declarations, or stop using the 'Exempt' label for non-behaviour verification commits.

findings.summary: _checkouts re-implements the 'git worktree list --porcelain' block parsing that commands.worktree_states already performs, so the porcelain rule lives in two places.
findings.evidence: adopt.py lines 33-45 and commands.py worktree_states (lines 144-151) both split porcelain output and read the 'worktree ' line (ENG-6).
findings.fix: Extract a helper in commands.py, for example worktree_checkouts(repo) yielding (path, branch), build worktree_states on it, and have adopt._checkouts call it.

findings.summary: The T006 New line names factory_cli.adopt._adopt_branch, which T008 renamed to _adopt_worktree with no New line for the current name.
findings.evidence: commit 9be7b4e (T006) records 'New: factory_cli.adopt._adopt_branch'; commit 57acb04 (T008) renames it to _adopt_worktree with no New line.
findings.fix: Accept it as a rename and record the rename in the retro, without rewriting history.
